8044.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁- (“to fill”) and closely related to Latin plēbs, though the exact pre-form of the term is unclear.

8039.t: πλανάω (planáō, “to wander”) + -της (-tēs, masculine agent noun suffix)

8088.t: From πρᾶγμα (prâgma, “a thing done, a fact”) + -ικός (-ikós).

8093.t: From πρεσβεύω (presbeúō, “to be elderly; to be ambassador”) + -εία (-eía, “nominal suffix”) and see πρέσβυς (présbus, “elder”).

8047.t: From πλησίον (plēsíon, “near”) + -άζω (-ắzō, “suffix for verbs”). Compare cognate πελάζω (pelázō) and old πιλνάω (pilnáō).

8030.t: From περι- (perĭ-, “beyond”) + -φρων (-phrōn, suffix for adjectives relating to the mind or emotions).

8061.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pol͏̌l͏̌ós, from Proto-Indo-European *pol-yós, from the root *pelH- (“pale, gray”).

8054.t: An o-grade verbal noun from the root of πλέω (pléō, “to sail”) + -ος (-os).

8038.t: Probably from a Proto-Indo-European *peysd- (“to squeeze”), and cognate with Sanskrit पीडयति (pīḍáyati). The Indo-European root may be a d-extension of *peys- (“to grind, crush”), though such an enlargement is strange.

8019.t: From περι- (peri-, “around”) + τειχίζω (teikhízō, “to build a wall”)

8042.t: From πλέων (pléōn, “more”) + ἑκ- (hek-) (the root of ἔχω (ékhō, “to have”) + -της (-tēs).

8083.t: From the o-grade of πέρθω (pérthō) + -έω (-éō, frequentative suffix).

8059.t: From ποίη (poíē), Epic/Ionic form of πόα (póa, “grass”), + -εις (-eis).

8046.t: From πλήρης (plḗrēs, “full, complete”) + φορέω (phoréō, “to bear, wear”).
